name: TUSB8041RGCR
title: Four-port USB 3.0 hub
summary: TUSB8041 is a USB 3.0 hub controller with one upstream port and four downstream ports. Upstream it links at SuperSpeed and high/full speed at once; downstream each port runs SuperSpeed, high, full or low speed, and the downstream speeds are capped by what the upstream link supports. It handles per-port or ganged power switching with over-current inputs, battery charging (CDP, DCP, divider modes), and takes its configuration from pin straps, OTP ROM, an I2C EEPROM or an SMBus host. It runs from 1.1 V and 3.3 V with a 24 MHz crystal or clock, in a 64-pin 9 mm VQFN.
key_figures: Multi transaction translator, 4 TTs, 4 asynchronous endpoint buffers per TT
VDD 0.99 V to 1.26 V (1.1 V nom); VDD33 3 V to 3.6 V
778 mA typ, 3.0 host with 4 SS devices in U0
49 mA typ with SS devices; 99 mA typ, 2 SS + 2 HS devices
24 MHz crystal or 1.8 V oscillator, ±100 ppm
Pin straps, OTP ROM, I2C EEPROM (100 kbit/s) or SMBus slave
VQFN-64 (RGC), 9.00 mm × 9.00 mm, 0.5 mm pitch, 6 mm thermal pad

notes: TUSB8041 is the commercial grade (0 °C to 70 °C) and TUSB8041I the industrial grade (-40 °C to 85 °C), both in the 64-pin RGC package.
TUSB8041RGCRG4 and TUSB8041RGCRG4.A are listed with -40 to 85 °C operating range and TUSB8041 marking.
An automotive-qualified version, TUSB8041-Q1, exists.

circuits.title: Upstream port
circuits.description: The upstream port on a USB 3.0 Type-B socket. VBUS is scaled into USB_VBUS by a 90.9 kΩ / 10 kΩ divider and bypassed with 10 µF. The SuperSpeed transmit pair reaches the socket through 0.1 µF series capacitors; the receive and USB 2.0 pairs are direct. GANGED and FULLPWRMGMTz are strapped low with 4.7 kΩ, giving switched power with individual control per port. The socket shield is a separate chassis node, tied to logic ground through 1 MΩ, 0.1 µF and 1 nF in parallel.
notes: J1 pins: 1 VBUS, 2 DM, 3 DP, 4 GND, 5 SSTXN, 6 SSTXP, 7 GND, 8 SSRXN, 9 SSRXP, 10 SHIELD0, 11 SHIELD1.

circuits.title: Downstream port 1
circuits.description: Downstream port 1 on a USB 3.0 Type-A socket. Switched VBUS (DN1_VBUS, from the power switch) passes a 220 Ω ferrite bead to the socket, with 0.1 µF on the socket side. The SuperSpeed transmit pair has 0.1 µF series capacitors; receive and USB 2.0 pairs run direct. A 4.7 kΩ pull-up to 3.3 V on PWRCTL1/BATEN1 enables battery charging on this port and is fitted only when charging is wanted; the same pin drives the switch enable, and OVERCUR1z takes the switch fault flag. The shield goes to chassis, tied to ground through 1 MΩ, 1 nF and 0.1 µF.
notes: J2 pins: 1 VBUS, 2 DM, 3 DP, 4 GND, 5 SSRXN, 6 SSRXP, 7 GND, 8 SSTXN, 9 SSTXP, 10 SHIELD0, 11 SHIELD1.

The SuperSpeed transmit pair has 0.1 µF series capacitors; receive and USB 2.0 pairs run direct. A 4.7 kΩ pull-up to 3.3 V on PWRCTL2/BATEN2 enables battery charging on this port and is fitted only when charging is wanted; the same pin drives the switch enable, and OVERCUR2z takes the switch fault flag. The shield goes to chassis, tied to ground through 1 MΩ, 1 nF and 0.1 µF.
notes: J3 pins: 1 VBUS, 2 DM, 3 DP, 4 GND, 5 SSRXN, 6 SSRXP, 7 GND, 8 SSTXN, 9 SSTXP, 10 SHIELD0, 11 SHIELD1.

The SuperSpeed transmit pair has 0.1 µF series capacitors; receive and USB 2.0 pairs run direct. A 4.7 kΩ pull-up to 3.3 V on PWRCTL3/BATEN3 enables battery charging on this port and is fitted only when charging is wanted; the same pin drives the switch enable, and OVERCUR3z takes the switch fault flag. circuits.description: Downstream port 4 on a USB 3.0 Type-A socket. Switched VBUS (DN4_VBUS, from the power switch) passes a 220 Ω ferrite bead to the socket, with 0.1 µF on the socket side. The SuperSpeed transmit pair has 0.1 µF series capacitors; receive and USB 2.0 pairs run direct. A 4.7 kΩ pull-up to 3.3 V on PWRCTL4/BATEN4 enables battery charging on this port and is fitted only when charging is wanted; the same pin drives the switch enable, and OVERCUR4z takes the switch fault flag. circuits.title: VBUS power switches
circuits.description: Two TPS2561 dual switches feed the four downstream VBUS rails from a 5 V board supply. Each channel's enable is driven by the hub's PWRCTL/BATEN pin for that port, and its fault output, pulled up to 3.3 V with 10 kΩ, drives the matching OVERCURz input. A 25.5 kΩ resistor on each ILIM pin sets the limit to 2.2 A per port. Each output carries 0.1 µF and 150 µF; each switch input has 0.1 µF.
notes: TPS2561 pins: 1 GND, 2 and 3 IN, 4 EN1, 5 EN2, 6 FAULT2Z, 7 ILIM, 8 OUT2, 9 OUT1, 10 FAULT1Z, 11 PAD.

circuits.title: Clock, reset and straps
circuits.description: A 24 MHz crystal across XI and XO with a 1 MΩ resistor in parallel and 18 pF from each side to ground. GRSTz has only 1 µF to ground, which is allowed when the 1.1 V rail is stable before the 3.3 V rail; the capacitor may need changing to suit the ramps. USB_R1 has its 9.53 kΩ 1 % reference resistor, TEST is pulled down with 4.7 kΩ, and AUTOENz is pulled down with 4.7 kΩ, enabling automatic charging mode. PWRCTL_POL is left open, so its internal pull-up selects active-high switch enables. The serial interface pins and SMBUSz are left open.

circuits.title: Supply decoupling
circuits.description: The eight VDD pins share one 1.1 V node fed from the board 1.1 V rail through a 220 Ω ferrite bead, with seven 0.1 µF capacitors and one 10 µF. The four VDD33 pins share a 3.3 V node fed through a second bead, with four 0.1 µF and one 10 µF. The thermal pad is ground and NC is left open.

where.TPWRON_EN: nominal time from PWRCTL turned off to PWRCTL turned on again
where.pwronTime: register F0h bits 3:1, used when the OTP pwronTime field is zero

operation.text: Upstream the hub connects at SuperSpeed and at high or full speed simultaneously. Downstream ports run SuperSpeed, high, full or low speed. On a high/full-speed-only upstream link the downstream SuperSpeed is off; on a full/low-speed-only upstream link both SuperSpeed and high speed are off downstream. The USB 2.0 side is a multi-TT hub with four transaction translators. No special driver is needed.

With individual control, the host switches each downstream port on and off, and an over-current shuts off only the port at fault. In ganged mode all ports are powered when any one needs power, stay on until every port can be turned off, and an over-current turns all of them off. Switching is enabled by fullPwrMgmtz (strap FULLPWRMGMTz), per-port or ganged is chosen by ganged (strap GANGED), and enable polarity by pwrctlPol (strap PWRCTL_POL).

Charging support is turned on port by port with batEn[3:0] in register 06h, whose defaults are the PWRCTL/BATEN strap levels. With the upstream port connected (VBUS above 4 V) an enabled port is a Charging Downstream Port (CDP). With it unconnected the port is a Dedicated Charging Port (DCP, also meeting YD/T 1591-2009), or, in automatic mode, switches between DCP and a divider mode that puts fixed DC levels on DP and DM for devices that look for them. The divider mode signals up to 5 W by default, or up to 10 W with HiCurAcpModeEn (register 0Ah). Port 1 has no CDP while automatic mode is on. Battery charging needs power switching enabled with individual port control.

Settings come from strap pins latched at GRSTz release, from one-time-programmable OTP ROM (VID, PID, removable ports, polarity, charging options, power-on delay; programmed through vendor-defined USB requests over the USB 2.0 upstream port), from an I2C EEPROM, or from an SMBus host. Custom strings and serial number come only from EEPROM or SMBus. The serial interface is active when SCL/SMBCLK and SDA/SMBDAT are both pulled up to 3.3 V at reset release; SMBUSz then picks I2C master (1) or SMBus slave (0).

As a single I2C master at 100 kbit/s the hub reads an EEPROM at 7-bit address 1010000b from offset 0. If byte 0 is 55h the registers are loaded from the EEPROM map; otherwise the hub drops out of I2C mode and runs on defaults, and with an unprogrammed EEPROM it enables a programming endpoint so the EEPROM can be written over USB. Bytes above offset 0Ah are needed only for options enabled in the two device configuration registers. The upstream port does not connect until loading is complete.

In SMBus mode the hub answers block read and block write only, at address 1000 1xyz with x and y from the GANGED and FULLPWRMGMTz straps; other protocols get no response. It waits with the upstream port disconnected until the host clears cfgActive in register F8h, and draws extra supply current while configuration is pending (SMBUS programming current: 79 mA VDD33, 225 mA VDD).

XI and XO drive an internal oscillator from a 24 MHz fundamental-mode crystal with 12 pF to 24 pF load capacitance, ±100 ppm or better, and ESR of 50 Ω at most; load capacitors are needed, valued per the crystal maker. An external clock instead goes to XI as a 1.8 V signal with XO open; it must be ±100 ppm or better with under 50 ps peak-to-peak absolute jitter, or under 25 ps after the USB 3.0 jitter transfer function. A 1 MΩ resistor goes across XI-XO with a crystal. Keep XI and XO short and away from switching traces, and keep the capacitance between them low, for example by guarding the load capacitors with ground.

VDD and VDD33 have no required order, and either may stay up alone indefinitely if all ratings are respected, bus contention with VDD33 up totals no more than 100 hours over life, and bus contention with VDD33 down can violate the absolute maximum ratings. GRSTz must stay low at least 3 ms after both rails are in range; a supervisor with programmable delay or an RC network can generate it. Each rail ramps in 0.2 ms to 100 ms. A capacitor-only reset requires VDD stable at least 10 µs before VDD33; if VDD33 settles first, reset must be driven actively.

After reset, with stsOutputEn set in register F0h, SS_UP and HS_UP show whether the upstream link is SuperSpeed or high speed, and SS_SUSPEND and HS_SUSPEND show upstream suspend; otherwise these pins are tri-stated.

VDD (1.1 V core) and VDD33 (3.3 V I/O) should each be one plane, and each can be separated from other rails by a ferrite bead. The core bead's DC resistance drops voltage at the core's high current: choose one under 0.05 Ω or adjust the regulator output. Every rail needs a 10 µF or 1 µF bulk capacitor, which can sit anywhere on the rail, while small decoupling capacitors sit right at the power pins, ideally two of different values per pin.

Each downstream port's VBUS needs a 5 V source good for up to 900 mA, switched by the hub's control pins or left permanently on, and at least 22 µF of low-ESR bulk capacitance to limit inrush. A ferrite bead in each port's VBUS is recommended for ESD and EMI, with 0.1 µF to ground on the connector side to shunt fast ESD current picked up from the cable.
Use a single board ground plane; the thermal pads of the hub and regulators connect to it with vias. Chassis or earth ground belongs on a separate plane near the USB connectors only, for EMI and ESD.

The 9.53 kΩ USB_R1 resistor sits as close to the device as possible, as does a 0.1 µF capacitor at each VDD and VDD33 pin and the crystal at XI/XO. The 100 nF SuperSpeed transmit capacitors and any ESD/EMI protection sit near the USB connector. Regulators go as far as possible from the hub, from the crystal and from the USB pairs, with their bulk capacitors close to them.
Pin pitch is 0.5 mm and the thermal pad 6.0 mm × 6.0 mm, grounded through an array of vias. Vias under the device other than thermal-pad vias should be covered with solder mask.

All USB pairs: 90 Ω ±10 % differential, each pair at least five trace widths from others or separated by ground, on one layer over unbroken ground, never over a plane split, no stubs (test points only in series and symmetric), as few bends as possible at 135° or more with left and right bends balanced, under eight inches long. Mismatch within a pair: under 5 mil for SuperSpeed, under 50 mil for USB 2.0; RX and TX pairs need not match each other. Keep vias few, identical for both lines and near the device. SuperSpeed pair polarity may be swapped freely; a swapped USB 2.0 pair needs its Px_usb2pol bit set. No power fuses across the pairs.
